stem.en: Milk turns to dahi overnight. Kabir says it is not a reaction "because nothing new is added, it is the same milk". What decides?

text.en: Whether grips have changed. Milk's sugar has been re-gripped into an acid by the microbes, which is why dahi is sour and thick. That is a reaction, even with nothing added.

feedback.en: The soda and the nimbu were two things, but a single thing can react on its own, like a firework or a rotting fruit. What counts is re-gripping.
The nail in copper sulphate did not fizz and was a reaction. Gas is one sign, not the only one.
Many reactions cannot easily be run backwards. Burning is one. That does not make them less of a reaction.

explanation.en: Look past what was added and ask what the atoms are doing. Dahi tastes different because different molecules are present, and different molecules means new grips.
